https://aa.com.tr/en/europe/ai-generated.text: Europe AI-generated 'Polish soldiers' part of coordinated anti-Ukraine disinformation campaign, fact-checkers warn Concerns coincide with growing strains in Polish-Ukrainian relations about historical memory, with recent disputes surrounding Ukrainian Insurgent Army in WWII Jo Harper 22 July 2026 • Update : 22 July 2026 VARŞOVA A coordinated disinformation campaign using artificial intelligence has emerged on Polish social media, spreading fabricated videos of supposed Polish soldiers criticizing Ukraine in what Ukrainian and Polish experts said is an attempt to undermine support for Kyiv and sow divisions among Western allies. Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation (CCD) wrote Tuesday on US social media platform X that the operation had been identified in the Polish-language information space and highlighted findings by Polish fact-checking organizations Demagog and Konkret24, which concluded that the videos were AI-generated. A network of accounts on YouTube, TikTok, Facebook and Instagram present themselves as "the voice of Polish soldiers," publishing short interview-style videos in which uniformed figures accuse Ukrainians of ingratitude, repeat false claims about high crime rates among Ukrainian refugees and exploit sensitive historical issues, including the Volhynia massacres, according to the CCD. The massacres were anti-Polish ethnic cleansings and mass murders by the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) and the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists during World War II. It said the campaign's objective was to weaken public support for Ukraine in Poland, damage trust between NATO allies and inflame existing political and historical tensions that Russia has repeatedly sought to exploit. The warning comes amid concern about Russian information operations targeting Poland. Earlier this month, analysts at Disinfo Digest said Kremlin-linked narratives had increasingly focused on Poland's military modernization, NATO cooperation and support for Ukraine ahead of the alliance's summit in Ankara. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys also said he expects more of his country's cybersecurity and counter-disinformation firms to establish a presence in the Philippines. "There will be more presence from the ones that are dealing with cyber tools, and also that are dealing with countering different propaganda narratives," Budrys told Philstar.com in an exclusive interview on July 23. Budrys noted that several of these firms utilize AI-enabled monitoring systems. Beyond commercial tools, Lithuania is also prepared to share its operational frameworks for security operations centers, cyber legislation, e-governance infrastructure and digital public services. Lithuania is in the highest-level tier, or Tier 1, in the International Telecommunication Union's latest edition of the Global Cybersecurity Index, released in 2024. Meanwhile, the Philippines is under Tier 2 ("advancing"), already a jump from its prior classification of Tier 3 in 2020. Organizing government, civil society vs hybrid threats Budrys, who said he has spent close to 25 years in the security sector, said a lesson from Lithuania's experience is to concentrate the work in a small number of institutions rather than parcel it out across agencies. "It has to be whole-of-government approach, meaning that everyone is responsible, but you cannot share it around and everyone is doing everything," he said. "Then it will be at the end too many people in the kitchen." Vilnius said he assigned core counter-hybrid tasks to defense and strategic communications agencies, while leaning heavily on civil society — which Budrys called the "highest added value" component of Lithuania's security apparatus. He highlighted Lithuania's volunteer online networks , organized as non-governmental organizations, that track and debunk pro-Kremlin narrative operations. "We were fighting trolls with 'elves,'" Budrys said. Lithuania has mapped how responsibilities are divided among Russian state institutions, state media, and state-enabled actors — including organized crime — and is willing to share that intelligence, Vilnius' top diplomat said. Budrys noted that Lithuania is similarly targeted by China. During his trip to Manila, Budrys also met with the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and denounced China's harassment of Philippine vessels as a breach of international law. The Lithuanian minister told Philstar.com that Lithuania was looking to share maritime security technologies refined during the war in Ukraine with the PCG. Photograph: Lane Turner/The Boston Globe/AP View image in fullscreen Arjun Aravind and his lawyer Debra DeWitt during his arraignment in Concord, Massachusetts, on Thursday. Photograph: Lane Turner/The Boston Globe/AP Massachusetts Massachusetts teen accused of killing mother and brother used ChatGPT District attorney says Arjun Aravind, 17, used internet and AI to search for fantasy stories regarding killing of his family Marina Dunbar Thu 13 Aug 2026 17.34 EDT Last modified on Thu 13 Aug 2026 18.14 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Massachusetts teenager accused of killing his mother and younger brother is being held without bail as authorities investigate a double-murder case that prosecutors say is connected to his use of ChatGPT. Arjun Aravind, 17, appeared Thursday morning for his arraignment in Concord district court, where a not-guilty plea was entered on his behalf to murder and several additional charges. Authorities allege Arjun killed his mother, 45-year-old Sudha Venkatesan, and his 14-year-old brother, Siddharth Aravind, inside the family’s home on Tuesday. The investigation began after the teenager’s tutor arrived for a scheduled appointment at the home Tuesday and “was unable to make contact with residents upon arrival”, prosecutors said. The teen’s father, who had last spoken with his wife before leaving for work that morning, then contacted police. Officers arrived at the residence and “located the two victims dead inside” shortly after 6.30pm, according to the district attorney. Officials said Siddharth’s body was discovered on the home’s first floor, while his mother’s body was found in the basement. As investigators examined what may have preceded the killings, authorities uncovered online activity they described as concerning. “The investigation has so far shown that Arjun had recently been demonstrating some concerning behavior, including using the internet and ChatGPT to make searches for theoretical ideas or fantasy stories regarding the killing of his family,” the Middlesex county district attorney, Marian Ryan, said in a press conference . Ryan said the teenager had planned the deaths of family members in the form of fantasy fiction. “He was engaged in the use of ChatGPT in creating fantasy stories, kind of the gothic novel kind of stories, asking questions, creating characters, asking what about this if this happened to that, and they seem to appear to relate to threats to his family,” she added. The official causes of death have not yet been determined, prosecutor Suzanne Wiseman said Thursday, according to CBS News , but she described what happened as a “physical and violent struggle”. “At this time, based on the evidence that was found at the scene, it was apparent that blunt force trauma was used in some fashion on both individuals,” Wiseman said. By the time the bodies were discovered, both Arjun and his mother’s vehicle, a 2014 green Honda Accord, were missing from the residence, officials said. Hours later, a search for them shifted about 13 miles (21km) away to Wayland after an alarm was triggered in a parking lot early Wednesday morning. Responding officers quickly connected the vehicle to the investigation. Arjun was found at approximately 3.40am inside his mother’s car and arrested. Investigators also recovered evidence from the vehicle that prosecutors say was connected to the scene at the family’s home. “A number of items were found in that car that correspond to the murder scene,” Wiseman said. Arjun faces two counts of murder, two counts of assault and battery on a household or family member, two counts of assault and battery, use of a vehicle without authority and theft of a motor vehicle. The Guardian has reached out to OpenAI , the parent company of ChatGPT, for comment. This is not the first time an AI chatbot has been connected to criminal acts. Earlier this year, Florida’s top prosecutor launched a criminal investigation into how OpenAI and its software tool ChatGPT may influence users’ threats of harm to themselves or others, including whether it “offered significant advice” to a gunman accused of conducting a mass shooting in the state last year. At the time, in a statement, a ChatGPT spokesperson said those shootings were a tragedy “but ChatGPT is not responsible for this terrible crime” and the tool had provided factual responses to questions with information that was broadly publicly available and “did not encourage or promote illegal or harmful activity”. https://www.dailypost.co.uk/news/north-w.text: Production crews for an upcoming Netflix drama on have been spotted on location in Denbighshire . The Woods is an eight-episode series adapted from a novel by US writer Harlen Coben. Co-star is former Coronation Street actress Michelle Keegan, once again reuniting with Netflix and Coben following the global success of Fool Me Once, which hit the streaming platform at the end of 2023. The thriller, from Manchester-based Quay Street Productions, features a barrister whose sister goes missing from a summer camp 25 years previously. Having rebuilt his life, the body of a man turns up which suggests there could have been more to his sister’s disappearance. Taking on the lead role of Paul “Cope” Copeland is The Love Hypothesis and Hedda actor Tom Bateman. Keegan, who also previously appeared in Brassic and Our Girl, will star alongside him as Lucy Silverfield. The Woods marks the 14th Coben adaptation for Netflix. Like the story’s hero, the author once worked as a counsellor at a summer camp and he said the 2007 book was “one of my most personal novels". He said: “The Woods’ is a haunting and very personal story. It has everything you expect from us — twisty, turning, gasp-inducing — but at the core is a story of old love and yearning.” Much of the series is being shot in northwest England. Earlier this week a shoot took place outside Manchester city centre for a scene involving a car valet service. Sign up for the North Wales Live newsletter sent twice daily to your inbox Actors including Keegan and Bateman were later seen on location in Knutsford in Cheshire, sharing a laugh between shots. Other filming sites have included Bolton’s Le Mans Crescent. Now production crews have been spotted in Ruthin . On Friday (August 21) a section of Llanrhydd Road was coned off for film trucks, though as yet there have been no sign of cast members. However Keegan is no stranger to North Wales, having filmed extensively in Conwy for hit comedy-drama Brassic. Scenes for the hit Sky One series were shot in places like Abergele , Llanfair Talhaiarn, Betws-yn-Rhos and Conwy Marina. With co-star Joe Gilgun, the actress posed for fans in Llandudno during a break from filming. Her last Harlan Coben project, “Missing You,” generated 107.5m global views and became one of Netflix’s most popular shows of 2024 – it was the most-watched series for the first half of that year. Also starring in The Woods is Tracy-Ann Oberman, Tom Allen and Mandeep Dhillon. They’ll be joined by Inbetweeners actor James Buckley , who appeared in the Channel 4 sitcom as Jay. Join the North Wales Live Whatsapp community now For his latest Netflix collaboration, Coben has said the cast represents an “embarrassment of riches”. No date has yet been revealed for when the show will hit screens. A Polish adaptation of the same novel was released globally on Netflix in June 2020.

https://www.dw.com/en/can-eu-and-india-w.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OodP Prefer DW on Google France, unlike other EU members, already has an established presence in the Indian Ocean Image: Paul-David Cottais/Marine Nationale/abaca/picture alliance Advertisement The European Union is vying for a larger role in Indo-Pacific security as the US finds itself on the back foot in the Eastern Hemisphere . India is among the regional powers looking for new allies. Its rising economy and increasingly global ambitions have pushed it into new forums and partnerships, including ever closer defense ties with the European bloc . In January this year, India and the EU signed a Security and Defense Partnership, followed by their first formal Security and Defense Dialogue in March. More meetings followed throughout the year, including the fifth Maritime Security Dialogue in Brussels last month. However, while both sides want to boost cooperation on maritime security, working together in the Indo-Pacific remains a challenge — India and European countries simply have different defense priorities. France a player in the Indian Ocean theater "Europe can be a credible defense partner of India, especially in the maritime theater in general and Indo-Pacific in particular," Mohan Kumar, a former Indian ambassador to France, told DW. But Europe's capacity to expand its role is constrained by other security crises . "European distractions such as the conflict in Ukraine, which is of existential importance for it, do detract from this objective and can be a limiting factor," he added. How Europe's defense sector is trying to gear up To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video France is a notable exception, given its established military presence in the Indian Ocean. "France, with its presence in Reunion Island and Mayotte, is already cooperating with India in the Indian Ocean theater and this cooperation can be intensified," added Kumar. Javed Ashraf, another Indian diplomat, said that France has been "a strong, trusted and consistent security partner across the full spectrum of defense cooperation." "What makes the partnership easier is the acceptance that the two may not always agree or be in a position to cooperate," said Ashraf. " France also stands out for India because [France] has currently no defense cooperation with Pakistan or with China." EU disunited on security? While France remains the EU's only nuclear power and maintains its strongest military force, a cooperation between Paris and New Delhi does not automatically translate into a coherent European security role across the Indo-Pacific. "Europe as an entity has very little role in the Indo-Pacific security despite the announcement of a strategy in 2025," said Tara Kartha, a former member of India's National Security Council Secretariat. She pointed to political differences among EU members as an obstacle to a coherent security outlook. Those differences were on display during the EU's October 15–16 summit in Brussels, when leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine, but also signaled disagreements over funding and national priorities . What can EU offer to India? This could also explain why, as India's defense ties with Europe keep expanding, much of that cooperation still takes place between New Delhi and individual European nations. Germany, Spain, Italy and Poland have all emerged as important partners. Why India wants German submarines To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Ashraf said Brussels could signal broader support for its member states' partnerships with India and provide access to EU-funded programs, boosting cooperation in areas such as maritime security, space, critical minerals, chips and defense technologies. "India is also becoming an important source of defense supplies for a re-arming Europe," the diplomat added. There may also be opportunities to share experience in emerging areas of warfare . "India could also access drone technology in light of valuable experience gained by Europeans in Ukraine," Kumar said. Germany , the EU's largest economy, is another important part of this relationship. Alongside France, it has become a defense partner for India, including through major equipment purchases . India could push for its relationship with Berlin to include industrial partnerships and technology development. But experts warn that closer defense ties should not be confused with a shared strategic outlook, as European countries have their own priorities. Russia and China as major obstacles The differences between Brussels and New Delhi are particularly clear when it comes to Russia and China . India still relies heavily on Russian equipment and technology, even as it seeks to diversify its defense supplies. European governments, meanwhile, have been engaged in a tense standoff with Russia since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine . How India has become Russia's trade lifeline To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video That creates a problem for those seeking to deepen defense industry ties. "Buying a few big-ticket defense items, such as Rafale fighter jets from France or submarines from Germany, is one thing," said Gulshan Sachdeva, a professor of European Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University in New Delhi. "However, integrating India's defense industry into the expanding European defense value chain is more challenging as long as Russia remains Europe's principal security concern." China presents a different but equally important challenge. For India, China is a rival and source of major security issues , including an ongoing border dispute. While the EU also sees China as a "systemic rival," its members differ in how they balance security concerns with their economic relationships with China. These differences complicate attempts to develop a shared assessment of Indo-Pacific threats. On a geopolitical level, India wants partnerships that strengthen its capabilities without requiring it to align fully with another power's strategic priorities . European governments are also weighing their regional ambitions against security demands closer to home. The US has moved much of its naval power out of the Indo-Pacific due to the conflicts in the Middle East Image: U.S. Navy/ZUMA/picture alliance Cooperation without a security umbrella The new India-EU partnership creates a framework for closer engagement, but it does not amount to a joint security commitment. Ashraf said the two sides could strengthen their mutual capabilities but were unlikely to exercise a visible influence on the global security order. For now, maritime domain awareness, information-sharing, defense technology and selective industrial cooperation offer more realistic prospects than a common security role of the EU and India across the Indo-Pacific.
